title.narrative: Implementation of the Regional Action Plan for Africa (2021-2027) & 4th Cycle PR

description.narrative:
Under Global Priority Africa, the Secretariat will implement and promote the Regional Action Plan 2021-2027 and Flagship Programme 3: Fostering cultural heritage and capacity development. It will support capacity building, the increase of African experts, and involve youth. The Secretariat will primarily support 11 countries with no properties on the WH List, assist 14 sites on the List of the WH in danger, mentoring experts and support conservation to achieve targets of the SDGs and Aspiration 5 of the Agenda 2063. Support will focus on the participation of the States Parties, the African World Heritage Fund, universities, experts, civil society, youth and other partners in celebrating the 50th anniversary of the 1972 Convention.
The World Heritage Committee, through Decision 46 COM 10B, requested the World Heritage Centre and its partners to continue monitoring the implementation of the Third Cycle Regional Action Plan (2021–2027) and to prepare a final assessment report on its overall implementation for submission to the Committee in 2028. Furthermore, through Decision 47 COM 10, the Committee launched the Fourth Cycle of Periodic Reporting in Africa and underscored the importance of building upon the achievements, lessons learned and recommendations emerging from the Third Cycle.
In this context, the budget allocated to the follow-up of the Third Cycle Regional Action Plan during the 2026–2027 biennium remains fully relevant and necessary. The proposed activities will not only support the completion of the Third Cycle by monitoring the implementation of the Regional Action Plan and documenting its results, but will also directly contribute to the successful implementation of the Fourth Cycle of Periodic Reporting in Africa.
As one of the first regions to implement the renewed Periodic Reporting approach, sub-Saharan Africa, comprising 47 States Parties and 112 World Heritage properties at the launch of the Fourth Cycle, will play a leading role in operationalising the reforms adopted by the Committee. The follow-up activities will provide an opportunity to assess the extent to which States Parties have integrated and implemented the priorities of the Third Cycle Regional Action Plan at national and site levels, while simultaneously identifying remaining capacity-building needs, institutional gaps and emerging priorities to be addressed through the Fourth Cycle.
The activities financed under this budget line therefore serve a dual purpose: (i) completing the monitoring and evaluation of the Third Cycle Regional Action Plan and informing the final assessment report to be submitted in 2028; and (ii) supporting the implementation of the Fourth Cycle by ensuring continuity of regional cooperation, strengthening national capacities, and providing an evidence-based foundation for the development and implementation of future regional priorities and action plans.
